```{r}
packages <- c(
  "ggplot2",         # Data visualization (histograms, QQ plots, diagnostic plots)
  "flexdashboard",   # 
  "shiny",           # for filters make sure graphs are reactive the filters and can be rendered
  "tidyverse"        # 
)

quiet_library <- function(pkg) {
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings({
    if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
      install.packages(pkg, dependencies = TRUE)
    }
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
  }))
}

# Install any that are missing
installed <- packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(!installed)) {
  message("Installing missing packages: ", paste(packages[!installed], collapse = ", "))
  install.packages(packages[!installed], dependencies = TRUE)
}

# Apply the function to load the packages 
invisible(lapply(packages, quiet_library))
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# library(flexdashboard)
# library(shiny)
# library(tidyverse)



atp <- read.csv("atp_number_1.csv")

#### creating the filtered data
filtered_data <- reactive({
  if(input$sex == "All"){
    atp   } else {    filter(atp, Sex == input$sex)  }})
```

Column    
-------------------------------------------
 


```{r}
# Creating the dropdown box filter
selectInput(
  "sex",
  "Select Sex",
  choices = c("All", unique(atp$Sex)))
```

### Number of Records in a KPI card
```{r}
# Number of records in a KPI card
renderValueBox({                   #### needs render value box to react to the filter
  valueBox(nrow(filtered_data()),"Records") })
```
### Age plot
```{r}
renderPlot({                              #### needs render plot to react to the filter
 ggplot(filtered_data(), aes(x = Age_years)) +
 geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white")+
 theme_minimal()})
```
### Task 1 - Add a second card showing average age.
```{r}
# Task 1 - Add a second card showing average age.

renderValueBox({                   #### needs render value box to react to the filter
  valueBox(round(mean(filtered_data()$Age_years), 1), "Average Age in yrs") })

```

### Task 2 - boxplot comparing age by sex.

```{r}
# Task 2 - Add a boxplot comparing age by sex.
renderPlot({                              #### needs render plot to react to the filter
 ggplot(filtered_data(), aes(x = Sex, y = Age_years, fill = Sex)) + # sex on x axis, age on y axis
 geom_boxplot() + 
 scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Set2') +
 labs(x="Sex", y = "Age (yrs)") +
 theme_minimal()})

```


### Task 3. chart showing players with more than 150 weeks at No. 1.

```{r}
# Task 3 - chart showing players with more than 150 weeks at No. 1.
# csv data just has number of weeks at number 1 form a start date, so will sort from that
renderPlot({                              #### needs render plot to react to the filter
 weeks150 <- filtered_data() %>% # using pipe operatr from tidyverse to pass output
  group_by(Player, Sex) %>%       # group by player and sex
  summarise(totalweeks = sum(Weeks)) %>%   # sum of weeks at number 1 per player
  filter(totalweeks > 150) %>%          # 
  arrange(totalweeks)
  
  # pick out the player column from the weeks150- dataframe, will keep the sorted order in the plot
  weeks150$Player <-factor(weeks150$Player, levels = weeks150$Player)

 ggplot(weeks150, aes(x = Player, y = totalweeks, fill = Sex)) +
 geom_col() + 
 coord_flip() +      #flip the bars to horizontal bars
 scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Set2') +
 labs(x="Player", y = "ttoal weeks at nunebr 1") +
 theme_minimal()})

```



### Task 4 - Chart showing the youngest 10 players to reach No. 1.

```{r}

renderPlot({                              #### needs render plot to react to the filter
 youngest10 <- filtered_data() %>% # using pipe operatr from tidyverse to pass output
  group_by(Player, Sex) %>%       # group by player and sex, one row per player
  summarise(agefirstno1 = min(Age_div_365.25)) %>%   # age when first became no. 1 
  arrange(agefirstno1)   %>%  # youngest first
  head(10)  %>%           # get firsst 10 records
  arrange(desc(agefirstno1)) # sort order
  
  # pick out the player column from the weeks150- datsaframe, will keep the sorted order in the plot
  youngest10$Player <-factor(youngest10$Player, levels = youngest10$Player)

 ggplot(youngest10, aes(x = Player, y = agefirstno1, fill = Sex)) +
 geom_col() + 
 coord_flip() +      #flip the bars to horizontal
 scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Set2') +
 labs(x="Player", y = "age when became World No.1") +
 theme_minimal()})

```

### Task 5. Which players have spent more than 150 cumulative weeks at World No. 1?

```{r}


# csv data just has number of weeks at number 1 form a start date, so will sort from that
# displying in table rather than chart for somethgin different 
# renderdatatable seems to be deprecated so will just use this version
# as per here > https://shiny.posit.co/r/reference/shiny/latest/
renderTable({                              #### needs render plot to react to the filter
 cumulwks150 <- filtered_data() %>% # using pipe operatr from tidyverse to pass output
  group_by(Player, Sex) %>%       # group by player and sex
  summarise(totalweeks = sum(Weeks)) %>%   # sum of weeks at number 1 per player
  filter(totalweeks > 150) %>%          # 
  arrange(desc(totalweeks))
  cumulwks150
}
)


```

```{r}
# will render in atable as per questio 5 as question very similar to question 4...s

  group_by(Player, Sex) %>%       # group by player and sex, one row per player
  summarise(agefirstno1 = min(Age_div_365.25)) %>%   # age when first became no. 1 
  arrange(agefirstno1)   %>%  # youngest first
  head(10)  %>%           # get firsst 10 records
  arrange(agefirstno1) # sort order

 }
```
